server.description: Live job listings from 20 ATS platforms plus SEEK, JobStreet, JobsDB, jobs.ch and The Muse
server.title: Snow Leo Jobs & Hiring

io.apify.authentication: OAuth with the user's own Apify account, or an Apify API token in the Authorization header
io.apify.billing: The connecting user's own Apify account is billed per result; there is no key to buy from the publisher

measured: Jobs read live from 20 applicant tracking systems including Greenhouse, Workday, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Oracle Cloud, BrassRing and UKG: 59,185 jobs in one run, with 1,045 company boards built in.
The SEEK family API stops at 500 jobs per query (page 6 at 100 rows returns an empty list); measured 1,500 unique jobs in 120 s from one run, zero duplicates, across 8 markets.
jobs.ch answers HTTP 422 at page 101, capping one query at 2,000 of the 46,121 jobs on the site; measured 2,400 unique jobs in 64 s, zero duplicates.
The Muse answers HTTP 400 at page 100, capping one query at 1,980 of 411,813 jobs; measured 2,060 unique jobs in 176 s, zero duplicates.

server.name: io.github.MagzhanSan/snowleo-leads
server.description: Local business leads from Google Maps, 7 directories, DuckDuckGo and OpenStreetMap, with contacts
server.title: Snow Leo Leads & Contacts

io.apify.authentication: OAuth with the user's own Apify account, or an Apify API token in the Authorization header
io.apify.billing: The connecting user's own Apify account is billed per result; there is no key to buy from the publisher

measured: Google Maps stops near 150 places per search view; an adaptive map grid returned 766 places against 160 for 'coffee' in Austin (4.79x) in 42 s and 168 requests, 12 Sep 2026.
Every page a human can click on BBB gives 175 unique businesses; bucketed queries returned 524 (Apify runs kt2dccRUXf2Itm2BL = 175, rKU71p8Dxq62dCgQ0 = 524).

DuckDuckGo local search runs on a different index: of 164 businesses returned across 10 category+city pairs, 82 (50%) were absent from Google Maps swept to its own ceiling; the website field was filled for 97.9% of rows against 79.7% in a Google Maps sample of 300 the same day, 16 Sep 2026.
OpenStreetMap sweep of Austin, Texas: 7,673 named businesses, 3,932 with no website at all, one Overpass query, 80.5 s. Manchester UK: 5,905 and 4,261 in 13.4 s.
Reading contact pages as well as the home page found an email on 57 of 135 live business websites against 31 from the home page alone.

server.name: io.github.MagzhanSan/snowleo-marketplaces
server.description: Priced listings from Amazon, Shopify stores, the App Store, Google Play, Airbnb and Redfin
server.title: Snow Leo Marketplaces & Prices

io.apify.authentication: OAuth with the user's own Apify account, or an Apify API token in the Authorization header
io.apify.billing: The connecting user's own Apify account is billed per result; there is no key to buy from the publisher

measured: One Amazon search stops at 306 products for 'wireless earbuds' while Amazon's own header claimed over 20,000; six price bands returned 96 products, 96 unique, zero overlap.
Of 47 live Shopify storefronts, 14 refuse /products.json on their own domain; reading the shop's Shopify origin recovered 10 of those 14, making 43 stores readable instead of 33.
Apple caps reviews at 500 per storefront per sort order (page 11 returns HTTP 400); opening both sort windows gave 937 unique reviews on one app with only 63 shared, across 59 storefronts.
Google Play keeps reviews in separate non-overlapping language piles: com.spotify.music on 13 Sep 2026 gave 10,800 distinct review IDs from 18 languages with 0 duplicates between them.

Airbnb search hands out at most 270 rows per query containing 227 distinct listings; on Paris, 13 Sep 2026, flat pagination gave 257 listings from 7 queries and an adaptive map grid gave 1,916 from 63 queries (7.46x) in 117 s.
Redfin's search endpoint has no pagination at all - page_number=2 returns page 1 byte for byte - and Redfin's own Download All CSV export stops at 350 listings.

Any public Telegram channel through its web preview, 68 fields per message including reactions counted per emoji, the channel numeric id, author signature, poll results, forwards, replies, inline buttons and direct CDN links to attachments, plus in-channel keyword search and handle lookup.
